trust_decision.summary: Before any filesystem call on an output path, the path's scheme (lower-cased, treated as 'file' when absent) must be in the single-entry allow-list ['file']; decided in AbstractGenerator::prepareOutput() through the new isProtocolAllowed() helper.

landing_point.why: The advisory names the output filename and a case-insensitive bypass of the phar:// check; this is the only phar-related string check in the tree and sits at the top of prepareOutput().

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report is about the output filename only; stylesheet/attachment are input option values, a different parameter, and that option path already has a scheme allow-list (isOptionUrl) so it reads as already protected.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: file:// output URLs and Windows drive-letter absolute paths are legitimate outputs today and must stay accepted; a fix that rejects any string carrying a scheme, or any string containing ':', breaks them (the published fix needs a dedicated Windows-drive-letter regex to avoid this).

O6_input_shapes: plain relative path with no scheme (out.pdf)
absolute local path with no scheme (/tmp/out.pdf)
Windows drive-letter path (single-letter scheme recognised by a regex, Windows only)
scheme case variants (phar://, PHAR://, PhAr://) folded to lower case
other wrappers rejected by the allow-list rather than a phar blacklist (php://filter, http://, https://, ftp://)
filenames parse_url() cannot parse, rejected as invalid

O8_uncovered_routes.route: stylesheet/attachment option values go straight into the isFile() wrapper before any scheme decision, so a phar:// value reaches \is_file() and can trigger PHAR metadata deserialization on PHP < 8.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Option values are not the output filename the report is about, and isOptionUrl() already allow-lists schemes for these options, so the value looks validated; in fact isFile() runs first in the same expression.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: 1 file (src/Pdf.php) from the landing point, same namespace and package

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the cache-folder option value routed through the same is_file()/mkdir() content-check handler
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is another path-valued option in the same configure() list as stylesheet/attachment, so a maintainer adding temp-path handling would copy handleArrayOptions().

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a re-added src/Image.php generator subclass with its own generate() override
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The README still names Pontedilana\PhpWeasyPrint\Image as a historical class; restoring it as a second generator in a new file is a natural extension, and an override of generate() can skip prepareOutput().

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a caller-supplied temporary folder/filename stat'ed with is_dir()/mkdir() in createTemporaryFile()
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: setTemporaryFolder() is already public and takes an untrusted path; a companion setter for the temp filename would stat that caller path before writing.

O9_family: CWE-502 deserialization of untrusted data reachable through PHP stream wrappers (PHAR metadata deserialization), incomplete blacklist on the output path

O10_build.toolchain: composer (php 7.4-8.5, psr/log, symfony/process) + PHPUnit 9.6, phpstan, php-cs-fixer for dev
O10_build.project_tests: tests/Unit/AbstractGeneratorTest.php and tests/Unit/PdfTest.php run against PdfSpy/getMockForAbstractClass, so no weasyprint binary is required, and the output-path/option tests are local. Caveat: two dataOptions cases (attachment http(s) URLs) fetch remote content, so those specific cases need network.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Case-fold the filename before the existing phar:// prefix check (or extend that blacklist with the other wrapper names) inside prepareOutput().

out_of_scope_notes: The pinned tree already carries two earlier security fixes in the same repo (SSRF/file disclosure via option URLs, src/Pdf.php:26-42; arbitrary deletion at shutdown, src/AbstractGenerator.php:326-344); they are outside this advisory but explain the existing isOptionUrl() scheme guard that makes the O8 route look protected.
unverified: repo_mb: no shell access in this session, so the size in MB was not measured; the tree is ~30 small text files with no vendor directory, which is why tiny_repo is asserted.

Whether tests/Unit/AbstractGeneratorTest.php::testFailingGenerateWithOutputContainingPharPrefix passes at the pinned commit: it mocks prepareOutput (so no exception is raised there) and then generate() reaches getEscapedBinary(), which should throw RuntimeException rather than the expected InvalidArgumentException.
present_in_latest for the O8 route: the input says no latest release exists, so it could not be checked.

Actual PHAR deserialization impact needs PHP < 8 and an attacker-uploaded .phar already on disk; the route itself (is_file() reached with a phar:// value before any scheme check) is verified from code, the end-to-end effect is not.
